scope: Inventory of missing physical elements at the selected E8 state. Candidate causes, not a demonstration of adequate physics or a new atmosphere.
already_present: Nonisothermal wind, variable composition and mean molecular weight, spherical continuity, linear stellar tide, thermal advection and expansion.
Multilevel H non-LTE, bound-free feedback, H-minus/molecular chemistry, metal heating/cooling including 716-level Fe II, selected Ly-beta/O I, local Ly-alpha/Fe and shared spherical IR transport.
Observer radial wind, prescribed rotation and day-to-night velocity shifts. Stellar pumping and subsequent spontaneous line emission already count resonant reemission.

formation_diagnostic.scope: Fixed E8, corrected existing n/l line centers, phase 0.375; not the processed phase coadd.
formation_diagnostic.peak_emission: About 86% of positive peak emission comes from 1.175 and 1.258 Rp, at 6492 and 7079 K. Their emission-weighted effective source/Planck ratios are about 0.887 and 0.384.
formation_diagnostic.core_emission: About 82% of positive core emission comes from 1.5125 Rp. This layer is hot (8163 K) but has source/Planck about 0.0594 and absorbs stronger radiation from below.
formation_diagnostic.conclusion: The thermal inversion exists. Its presence alone does not set line brightness; population ratios, radiation transport and geometry remain consequential.

candidates.missing: Nonlocal photoionization/fluorescence by escaped ordinary H and metal line photons, outside explicitly resolved groups.
candidates.reference_relation: Concrete native/C23 difference: C23 transports outlin into its summed photoionizing field; native ordinary destruction packets are local.
candidates.possible_effect: Redistributes ionization and thermal deposition between layers; the sign of the H-alpha response is unknown.
candidates.screen: The saved upper-column continuum optical depth is only 0.000411 at H-alpha and 0.01837 at Ly-alpha. H-alpha cannot photoionize n2; Ly-alpha can. Whole-column depths are 0.1007 and 591.4, respectively. This points toward lower absorption, and does not establish a large upper-layer response or an angular escape fraction.
candidates.discriminator: Tag escaped sources, screen receiver thresholds/columns, then a conservative fixed-state transport control excluding already counted local destruction and resolved groups.

candidates.missing: General cross-species overlapping-line shielding and full spatial/angular/frequency transport with bulk-velocity feedback into level rates.
candidates.reference_relation: C23 includes generic overlapping opacity; full moving-medium line transfer is also absent from the ordinary escape-probability reference closure. Both selected ordinary-line pumps omit bottom-to-upper continuum: their forward/outward diffuse field travels away from the star, toward smaller planetary radius. Native continuum bound-free transfer is already bidirectional.
candidates.possible_effect: Changes stellar pumping, trapping and the height where the H-alpha source drops. A returned line field might fill the core rather than increase the peaks.
candidates.discriminator: Rank foreign opacity in dominant energy channels; test selected H-line transfer at fixed populations, replacing the existing escape/pump ownership without adding duplicate scattering.

candidates.missing: Curved observer paths, off-limb emission, angular gas-state variations and dynamically determined horizontal/Roche flows.
candidates.reference_relation: Largely shared with the paper's plane-parallel, uniform-dayside observer; this is not automatically a cause of a paper-reproduction mismatch.
candidates.possible_effect: Changes emitting area, self-absorption and velocity weighting, hence peak amplitudes, red/blue contrast and phase variation.
candidates.discriminator: First a fixed-state spherical disk/halo decomposition with occultation by the opaque planet; then physically specified multi-column illumination/state controls if consequential.

candidates.missing: A self-consistent lower thermal/radiation domain and planet-view, phase-dependent stellar illumination including gravity darkening and rotation.
candidates.reference_relation: Native lower LTE cells and dark atmosphere boundary coexist with a 4500 K observer boundary. Exact author lower inputs are unavailable. A fixed PHOENIX star is a shared approximation.
candidates.possible_effect: Changes photons reaching emitting/absorbing layers and the thermal/NLTE transition. Extra irradiation does not necessarily increase neutral-H emission.
candidates.discriminator: Keep lower-photon ownership explicit; use the one-versus-two LTE-cell response and source-consistent boundary tests. Stellar gravity-darkening amplitudes require a planet-view SED calculation, not the local stellar brightness contrast.

candidates.missing: Advected ionization/excitation/chemical populations and consistently coupled material internal energy.
candidates.reference_relation: Population advection is also omitted in published stock sunbather; thermal advection is already included here.
candidates.screen: At 1.51/1.94 Rp, frozen ionization relaxation divided by neutral-gradient flow time is 0.00132/0.0232. n3 exit times are below a microsecond. Delayed n3 excitation is therefore a low-priority peak explanation on this state, not a globally excluded effect.
candidates.discriminator: Conservative frozen-field species transport, followed by consistent reaction/internal-energy bookkeeping before a coupled response. Do not append latent heat to the existing kinetic ledger independently.

candidates.missing: Selected excited He/metal/chemical states, H-alpha pressure broadening, nearby metal blends, nonthermal and external mechanical channels.
candidates.reference_relation: Mixed native reductions and shared limitations; each channel needs its own quantitative scope.
candidates.screen: The strongest nearby Fe II line has only 0.00324/0.000441 of H-alpha opacity in the two principal emitting cells. Existing He and minor-coolant controls do not identify a dominant missing source. The adopted spectrum has little hard-photon power; this does not establish the real star's XUV flux.
candidates.discriminator: Select channels using actual formation-region rate/energy/opacity budgets. Retain pressure-broadening obligations; do not use a small electron-scattering budget to dismiss resonant redistribution or off-limb light.

assessment_effect: Attach known missing elements and discriminators to the existing unknown reduction/observation Assessments. No status, criterion, historical Decision or equation is changed. Numerical convergence does not discharge these physical obligations.
